summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a five-day history of watery, non-bloody diarrhea and dehydration, following a trip to visit a friend's son at college. She had no fever or vomiting but reported lower abdominal cramping and dry mouth. Given her immunosuppressed state from kidney transplant and history of C. difficile, stool studies were performed, all of which returned negative. Abdominal imaging showed air-fluid levels consistent with diarrhea but no megacolon or obstruction. She was treated supportively with IV fluids and electrolyte repletion. Her diarrhea resolved, potassium normalized, and kidney function improved. She was discharged home with instructions to restart her antihypertensive medications gradually and follow up with her nephrologist. The episode was most consistent with viral gastroenteritis.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
